discover_full_text.description: Given a DOI, find a link to a freely readable copy. CORE looks through its own index and then outside it, so this answers 'is there a version of this paper anyone can read' for a DOI that is otherwise behind a paywall. A DOI with no free copy comes back as 'found: false' rather than failing, so a reading-list workflow can branch on it.

get_data_provider.description: Fetch one repository or journal in full: its name and institution, its OAI-PMH endpoint and metadata format, the software it runs, its location, its ROR and OpenDOAR identifiers, and its aliases. Takes a CORE ID or 'opendoar:<id>'.

parameters.description: The repository or journal to look up: its numeric CORE ID, or 'opendoar:<id>' to use its OpenDOAR ID instead. 'Search data providers' returns the CORE ID on every record.

results.title: CORE: three access levels to underpin open access

parameters.name: query

get_data_provider_stats.description: How much content a repository has contributed: metadata records, and how many of those CORE holds full text for. Leave the extras off for the headline counts, which is the cheaper call. Turn any of them on and CORE returns the fuller picture instead: the deposit history over time, the per-source breakdown, or one OAI set.

parameters.description: The journal to look up, by ISSN or by its CORE identifier. An ISSN works with or without its hyphen. CORE identifiers are prefixed, for example 'oai:doaj.org/journal:<id>'.

description: Search and read CORE, the world's largest aggregator of open-access research: over 300 million papers harvested from repositories, preprint servers and journals. Find works and the repositories holding them, follow a DOI to a free copy, count a field's output by year or author, and find research related to a paper.
